clauses.clause: Sole clause: trust period on Kiowa, Comanche, Apache and Wichita allotments expiring in calendar year 1926 extended ten years
Exceptions: 50 named allottees (33 Kiowa-Comanche-Apache, 17 Wichita) left out of the extension; no command, their trusts expired in 1926 under prior terms

PD-INDIAN.md M9 quotes sec. 13 as enacted and does not mention that a 1990 amendment removed sec. 2 from the proviso (per the 25 U.S.C. 5118 page); this does not change EO 4398, whose term ended in 1936, but matters for periods running in 1990.
Slice title has a run-together word ('allotmentsmade') and the president field is empty; the text shows Calvin Coolidge.

moves.note: Two held originals agree. The single command extends for ten years trusts expiring in 1926; the term ran out in 1936 under the order's own words.
One operative clause (the extension) plus a list of 50 excepted allottees that commands nothing; the clause ended not later than 1936-12-31.

IRA sec. 13 as enacted in 1934 (48 Stat. 986) was read only through the project doctrine file and the amended U.S.C. text; the order that took over the 1936 expiries is not identified; individual allotment expiry dates are not held.

propositions.claim: The GPO slip-order printing holds the order, signed by Coolidge on March 18, 1926.
propositions.quote: It is hereby ordered , under authority contained in Section 5 of the Act of February 8, 1887 (24 Stat . 389 )

propositions.claim: The ProQuest replica of the State Department copy carries the same text and the number.
The order extends only trusts expiring in 1926, and only for ten years, so its term ends in 1936.
propositions.quote: which trust expires during the calendar year , 1926, be, and is hereby extended for a period of ten years , with the following exceptions

propositions.quote: Allottees on the Wichita Reservation [...] 960 Nancy Long (deceased )

propositions.claim: The project doctrine holds that IRA sec. 13 kept sec. 2 from continuing periods for the listed Oklahoma tribes, so EO 4398's stated end stands.
propositions.quote: So for an order whose text names a listed tribe in Oklahoma, the order's stated end stands (EO 3363, 4281, 4384, 4398

propositions.claim: The current 25 CFR chapter I appendix lists E.O. 4398 (Mar. 18, 1926) under Kiowa, Comanche, Apache and Wichita as a past ten-year extension; it is a historical list of citations.

propositions.claim: The appendix says reservations without an asterisk depend on later instruments for extension, so later extensions are separate instruments.

propositions.claim: The project doctrine treats later blanket extension orders as new instruments, not continuations of the earlier order.
propositions.quote: Each is a new instrument running from the expiry of the period it extends.

review.conclusion_reason: The ten-year extension of 1926 expiries supports NO under own_terms, with the historical Oklahoma exclusion supported by the quoted doctrine and the statutory amendment history. No express ending was found in the reviewed sources; that formal-status statement remains a bounded search result. The exceptions merely limit coverage: their asserted 1926 expiry and March 18 ending are not established.
missed_evidence: The held GPO and ProQuest texts list 32 Kiowa-Comanche-Apache exceptions and 18 Wichita exceptions, not 33 and 17. Neither establishes actual expiry of excluded trusts or an ending on March 18, 1926.

The cited CFR appendix, General Orders table, confirms EO 7206's number, October 14, 1935 date, Oklahoma-only scope and ten-year period; PD-INDIAN.md's EO 7206 row identifies 1936 expiries. Its application to these particular allotments remains a candidate, but number and date are not unconfirmed.
review.stop_code_verdict: confirmed: WEB fits the first gap, which specifically requests an original printing of the historical statute; the evidence slice identifies held originals of the executive order, not that statute. The doctrine's quotation and Cornell amendment note narrow but do not fulfill that original-printing request.
review.suspected_defect: The exception clause misallocates the 50 exceptions as 33/17 instead of 32/18 and converts exclusion from this extension into an unsupported finding of actual trust expiry, with an inconsistent order-date ending.

verdicts.reason: Held GPO printing contains the quoted opening, CALVIN COOLIDGE, and March 18, 1926.
Held ProQuest OCR confirms the operative text, date, and [No. 4398].
The original expressly extends trusts expiring during 1926 for ten years, supporting a stated-term outer bound of December 31, 1936.
The original lists excepted allottees and includes 960 Nancy Long (deceased). This supports exclusion only, not the separate assertion that their trusts actually expired.
PD-INDIAN.md M9 contains the quoted conclusion and specifically includes EO 4398. Confirmed as the doctrine's position; it is not an original statutory printing.
The cited section lists all four tribes; its amendment note confirms removal of section 2 in 1990. The current proviso itself does not exclude section 2.
The appendix lists EO 4398 under the four tribes, dated March 18, 1926, with a ten-year extension. Its historical citation does not independently establish present operation.

The appendix states that unstarred reservations depend on statutes or executive orders for extensions. This supports the need for additional instruments, not an independent finding that EO 4398 ended.
PD-INDIAN.md M3 contains the quoted sentence characterizing subsequent extensions as new instruments.
